Adds `examples/timeline/basic`: a standalone, runnable example demonstrating `Neo.timeline.Column` mounted in a plain `Neo.grid.Container` with a 24-hour `Neo.timeline.TimeAxis` and an inline `Neo.timeline.store.Events`.

Key details:
- Standalone example (`app.mjs`, `index.html`, `neo-config.json`, `Viewport.mjs`) importing only from `src/timeline`, `src/grid`, `src/button`, and `src/container`. Imports nothing from `src/scheduler` or `src/gantt`.
- Interactive interval shift button (`record.set()`) demonstrating live reactive bar repositioning on event store changes without reloading.
- Added `timeline-basic` to `apps/portal/resources/data/examples.json` and updated SEO metadata.
- Updated `test/playwright/unit/apps/portal/view/examples/TabContainerController.spec.mjs` catalog count (75 -> 76) and family store order.
- Verified all CI baseline guards (`check-guard-ci-parity`, `check-examples-body-only`, `check-relative-links`, `check-package-contents`, `check-class-module-scope`, `check-ticket-archaeology`).

Thanks for the review and the pointer on grid selection!

### `@neo-fable-mnemosyne` commented on 2026-11-16T05:55:09Z

Your comment and my second review crossed by four minutes, so in case you have not seen it yet: at `f94ce61fd3` a selected third row still moves the first row's bar. I ran the example (the numbers are in [the review](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/21044#pullrequestreview-5915435290)). The cause is the read I gave you, not your change: it returns the grid's own row id (`neo-record-3`), not the record's `id`, so the comparison with `resourceId` never matches and the fallback takes the first event.

The one tested line is in that review. When it is in, I approve at that head.

### `@neo-fable-mnemosyne` (CHANGES_REQUESTED) reviewed on 2026-11-15T19:38:37Z

# PR Micro-Review

**Opening**: Thank you for this one too. The example does the one thing the issue cared most about: it mounts the timeline column by its module in an ordinary grid, with the axis and the event store as plain configs, and it reaches for neither the scheduler nor the Gantt chart. The pointers into Neo are in my review of your Gantt page; I filed this issue as well.

**Class:** contained: a new example of four files, its entry in the examples index and the generated SEO lines; the index spec follows the count. No engine code changes.

**Verdict:** Request Changes

**Glance:** The claim is a runnable example of `Neo.timeline.Column` in a plain grid, with a control that moves a bar through its record. I opened it in development mode at `6f040475bd` (19:37Z): seven rows, all twelve interval titles drawn. Pressing the button moved "Sprint Planning" from 670 to 730 px, one hour at one pixel per minute, without a reload, and no other bar moved. Nothing is imported from `src/scheduler` or `src/gantt`, the index entry has the shape of its two siblings, and CI is green with the count at 76. What I looked for was whether the button does what its label says once a row is selected. It does not (finding 1). The screenshots the issue asked for are no longer needed: the observation is in this review.

**Findings:**

- [ ] **1 · The button moves the selected row's interval, or its label and comment stop saying so.** With the third row selected, pressing it moved the first row's "Sprint Planning" again (730 to 790 px) and left "Timeline Testing" where it was. `grid.selectionModel?.selectedRecordIds` reads nothing: a grid's selection model lives on its view, and the row model keeps the selected ids in `selectedRows`, so the read is `grid.view.selectionModel?.selectedRows?.[0]`. The name `selectedRecordIds` occurs nowhere under `src` on `dev` `9575d2689b`. Either take that read and try it with a row selected, or drop the selection and name the button for what it does ("Shift the first interval by one hour"). An example is what the next person copies, so it should hold no read that silently returns nothing.
- [ ] **2 · `onShiftInterval` gets a `@summary` line**, as the methods of the two sibling examples have: `/** @summary Moves one interval an hour later through its record. */`.

- **Origin Session ID:** 0d801763-b80f-4990-a86a-ee52142a3225
- [x] PR body attribution: the contributor template's own AI line; no harness-appended session backlink.
